name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A motorcycle, including a motor scooter, whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (about 3,750 W). An electric two-wheeler that goes faster than a motorized pedalcycle's 25 mph, or has no pedals, but stays within that power is a motor-driven cycle. Defined by Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes Title 75 §102.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle: a seat or saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (about 3,750 W)

Riders need a Class M license, or one with a motor-driven cycle endorsement, and must be 16 or older; a Class C license covers only one with an automatic transmission and a cylinder capacity of 50 cc or less
Riders under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet, as must older riders unless they've held a motorcycle license for two years or completed an approved rider safety course
Registered with PennDOT for $9 a year, with the registration card carried while riding, and must carry insurance; exempt from titling
Kept off sidewalks and bike lanes
One whose motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower is a motorcycle
